subject: Helio renewal: geo expansion & migration credit - orderform redlines
messages:
From: Sophia Li <sophia.li@heliocorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@heliocorp.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helio renewal redlines + geo expansion order form

Jonas —

Thanks for the call last week. Attached are Helio's initial redlines to the renewal paperwork (MSA + order form). Two items we need your help on urgently: 

1) Geo expansion / migration credit: we plan to move 30% of our workload to EU regions at month 6. We'd like a migration credit to avoid double-billing for the overlap period (proposed credit table attached).

2) Term length & phased ramp: our finance team prefers a 24-month term with a phased capacity ramp (months 1-6: base, 7-12: +30%, 13-24: sustained). Would Redwood accept this sequencing in the order form?

I've copied our contracts team (contracts@heliocorp.com) and Marco Ruiz in finance for visibility. Doc attached: Helio_Renewal_Redlines_v1.docx (redline + summary).

Can you confirm receipt and share a plan for legal redlines and an updated order form we can review?

Best,
Sophia Li
Senior Counsel, HelioCorp

Attachments: Helio_Renewal_Redlines_v1.docx (docx, 78 KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Li <sophia.li@heliocorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helio renewal redlines + geo expansion order form

Sophia — thanks, got it. 

Quick summary of next steps from our side: 
- I'll coordinate with Sales Ops to incorporate the phased ramp into the order form and model the pro-rated billing impact.
- Ben (cc'd) will propose the capacity numbers and pricing tiers for the ramp.
- Laura (cc'd, Legal Ops) will review the MSA redlines and propose language for the migration credit and any region-specific data routing terms.

Questions for you up front so we can be efficient: 
- For the migration credit, is Helio proposing a fixed $ credit per migrated token/hour, or a % credit applied to overlapping capacity for the partial month? The redline doc had a table but I want to confirm the preferred mechanism.
- Any data residency or encryption requirements tied to the EU pop that we should codify?

I'll attach my quick notes and a checklist so we can track open items. Planning to have a revised order form + annotated MSA back to you by EOD 3/4 for discussion.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity proposal + orderform draft for Helio

Sophia / team —

Per Jonas' note, I ran the numbers for the phased ramp and sketched a proposed order form. Key points: 
- Base (months 1-6): 1.0x baseline capacity (same as current committed)
- Ramp (months 7-12): +30% additional reserved capacity; we'll convert to sustained capacity months 13-24 at +20% baseline (Helio can burst beyond reserved per existing burst rules)
- Pricing: tiered unit price for reserved capacity; the incremental +30% carries a 10% discount vs on-demand pricing for the ramp window.

Migration credit (to address overlap billing): we suggest a % credit on the incremental usage in the overlap month(s). Table in orderform-draft.xlsx shows %s and example math. Open to fixed-credit model if Helio prefers.

I've attached a clean order form (orderform-draft.xlsx) with the ramp schedule, pricing, and the credit table. Please review and flag any finance/legal constraints.

If acceptable, I'll bake these numbers into the order form and Laura can propose the actual clause language for the credit.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachments: orderform-draft.xlsx (xlsx, 54 KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Li <sophia.li@heliocorp.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helio renewal redlines + geo expansion order form — legal review

Sophia / Ben / Jonas —

Thanks for the materials. I reviewed Helio_Renewal_Redlines_v1.docx and Ben's order form draft. High-level legal positions and proposed edits below; attached is an annotated MSA with tracked changes (Redwood_MSA_annotated.docx).

1) Migration credit (suggested clause):
- Proposed wording: "If Customer migrates committed workload to a new geographic region and experiences overlapping billed capacity during the migration month(s), Redwood will apply a migration credit equal to X% of the incremental reserved capacity charges for the overlap period as set forth in the Order Form."
- We should avoid a per-token metric in the MSA; better to keep the calculation in the order form table (clean separation of pricing mechanics).

2) Data residency & encryption:
- If Helio requires EU data residency, we need to add an exhibit specifying the region and that the customer is responsible for routing to the region. Also include the encryption-at-rest KMS note if they're bringing their own KMS.

3) Term length / termination:
- 24-month term is acceptable from Redwood if Helio agrees to the phased ramp and the committed minimums are set in the order form. If they want early termination rights tied to migration (e.g., move from US to EU), we need to cap any early termination credits and define the notice period.

4) Contractual ambiguity:
- Several of Helio's redlines remove the "Reserved Capacity" definition; please keep that definition intact and map all pricing/credits back to that defined term.

Open items for Helio: please confirm preference for (a) % credit vs fixed credit, and (b) whether the KMS/encryption exhibit is required.

I'll push the annotated MSA + redlined order form to the Drive link and can prepare a short clean addendum language to attach to the order form once we have Helio's answers. Target: revised paperwork circulated by EOD 3/5.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Legal Operations — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_annotated.docx (docx, 110 KB)
